ClientResponses.Response:
Thank you for your feedback. We are sorry to learn that your burners are not lighting as expected. It sounds like there could be an issue related to gas flow, and we are here to help. 

Please perform a soapy water leak test as detailed in your grill owner's guide to rule out a gas leak. 

The lighting procedure is important to avoid triggering your grill's safety bypass mechanism. Here's how to light your grill:

Open the lid

Make sure all knobs are in the off position

Turn your LP tank on all the way

Wait 60 seconds *Very Important*

Turn the first burner to start/high

Hit your igniter

Turn on remaining burners one at a time and set each to high

Close the lid

Let your grill preheat to 450°F

Our Specialist team is here to help. Please look for our email outreach soon. Thank you!

Results.ReviewText: Not gonna lie, not my favorite Weber.  I’ve only ever owned Weber grills; my Genesis gave up after 18 years and I needed a new grill but a smaller one.  Before the Genesis I had the kettle style charcoal grill which did fine.  The Spirit is very touchy.  Had a hard time getting it to fire up the first time.  You have to turn the tank on really slow, otherwise it shuts down and won’t light. Also, my first tank was about 1/4 full and I had to get a new one.  After that it came on fine.  Also, a big negative is that the Spirit doesn’t have a tank monitor to let you know how much gas is left in the tank.  That’s a big negative for me.  Overall, still like Weber but this isn’t my favorite.
Results.Title: Needs a tank monitor.
